what_it_does: SmartNICs (network interface cards with their own processors, used in data centers to offload network management tasks from the main server CPU) often run several network functions side by side — for example, a firewall, a load balancer, and an encryption engine all on one card. These co-located programs compete for the same limited resources (processor cores, memory bandwidth, DMA engines that move data between chip and memory, and packet queues), causing each other to slow down in ways that are hard to predict. This paper builds a prediction model that takes as input the current resource allocation across all co-located programs and the rate and pattern of network traffic, and outputs the expected throughput and latency for each program. The goal is to give operators a tool to plan resource assignments on a SmartNIC so that each network function meets its performance target without accidentally starving another.
